summary: Knight-Hennessy Scholars gives full funding for any full-time Stanford graduate degree (MS and PhD to MBA, JD and MD) plus a leadership programme. You apply to Knight-Hennessy and, separately, to your Stanford degree programme. Winners are recent graduates from any country who show independent thinking, purposeful leadership and a civic mindset.
lookfor: Independence of thought: you think critically and form your own views
Purposeful leadership: you lead people toward meaningful goals with clear direction
Civic mindset: you take responsibility for your communities and act to improve them
A personal story that only you could have written
Admission to a full-time Stanford graduate programme (decided separately by that programme)
cycle: The 2027-cohort application closed on 6 October 2026 (1:00pm Pacific Time); the Stanford programme application is due by the programme's deadline or 1 December 2026, whichever is earlier. Video invitations go out in January, all applicants hear by 27 January 2027, finalists have a Zoom interview in mid-February and attend Immersion Weekend on 5–6 March 2027, and scholars are notified on 16 March 2027. The 2028-cohort application opens in summer 2027 with a deadline expected in early October 2027 — use this guide to prepare.

eligibility.q: Did you earn your bachelor's degree recently enough? (2027 cohort: January 2020 or later; January 2018 or later with military service. The window moves forward each year — check for 2028.)
eligibility.no: You are outside the window. Consider Gates Cambridge, Chevening or Commonwealth awards, which have no graduation-year limit.

eligibility.q: Will you apply to (or already hold a deferred offer for) a full-time Stanford graduate programme starting in the same year?
eligibility.no: You must be admitted to a Stanford full-time graduate degree to become a scholar. Programmes like the Honors Cooperative Program, MLA, JSD and MLS are not eligible.

eligibility.q: Does your bachelor's degree count as equivalent to a US bachelor's for your Stanford programme?
eligibility.no: Check your Stanford programme's admission page and confirm with the department that your degree is treated as equivalent.

eligibility.q: Can you meet your programme's English requirement (TOEFL/IELTS, if it requires one)?
eligibility.no: Book a test early. Stanford generally asks for IELTS 7 or TOEFL 90 (older format), but programmes differ.

steps.title: Check eligibility and choose a Stanford programme
steps.why: You need two applications: one to Knight-Hennessy and one to a Stanford degree programme. Without admission to the programme you cannot become a scholar.
do: Open the eligibility page and check your bachelor's date against the cutoff.
Browse Stanford graduate programmes and pick the one that fits your goals.
On the programme page, note its deadline (KHS applicants must apply by it or by 1 December, whichever is earlier), test requirements (GRE, TOEFL/IELTS) and fee.
Note the KHS deadline (early October) in your calendar.
tips: MBA applicants must use Round 1 to stay eligible.
avoid: Assuming KHS admission means Stanford admission — they are separate.
check: I am inside the degree-date window and have a target programme.

steps.title: Understand the three criteria
steps.why: Your essays, recommenders and interviews are all judged on independence of thought, purposeful leadership and civic mindset.
do: Open the evaluation page and write the three criteria down.
For each, list three stories from your life.
Read the reflection questions page and answer them in a notebook.
tips: KHS cares about who you are, not just what you have done.
avoid: Writing a list of achievements without showing your thinking.
check: I have stories for all three criteria.

steps.title: Build your timeline and register
steps.why: The KHS deadline is early October, months before most Stanford programme deadlines — you must be ready early.
do: Register on the KHS 'future scholars' list for updates.
Put reminders for when the application opens (summer), 60 days, 30 days and 7 days before the October deadline.
Book GRE/TOEFL/IELTS dates if your programme needs them, leaving time for a retake.
When the application opens, create your account on the KHS portal.
tips: You can submit late test scores through your status page if needed.
avoid: Planning around the Stanford programme deadline instead of the earlier KHS one.
check: Dates are in my calendar and tests booked.

steps.title: Prepare résumé, transcripts and test scores
steps.why: KHS accepts unofficial transcripts, but your one-page résumé is the first thing readers see.
do: Write a one-page US Letter résumé in reverse-chronological order: education, work, activities, interests. No photo, no hyperlinks.
Scan your transcripts (unofficial is fine for KHS); get an official English translation if not in English.
Request official transcripts for your Stanford programme if it needs them (Nigeria: registry/transcript portal; budget weeks and naira fees).
Send test scores to Stanford if your programme requires them.
tips: Use the résumé for headlines and context — e.g. 'one of 3 First Class graduates out of 150'.
avoid: A two-page CV — KHS asks for one page.
check: One-page résumé and transcripts ready to upload.

links.t: Watch: How to WIN the Knight Hennessy Scholarship to STANFORD (Jack Anderson)

steps.title: Short answer 1: your intentions
steps.why: Shows you have a direction and how Stanford fits it.
do: State your short-term academic goal (the Stanford degree) and what you will do with it.
State your long-term professional aim in one clear sentence.
Connect the two with a reason rooted in your experience.
tips: Be specific about the problem you want to work on.
avoid: Generic 'I want to be a global leader' language.

links.t: Watch: Successful Application Tips from Knight-Hennessy Scholars! (Stanford)

steps.prompt: Describe your short-term and long-term academic and professional intentions.

steps.title: Short answers 2 and 3: experiences and improbable facts
steps.why: These show your character — openness to other views, courage, honesty about failure — and your personality.
do: Q2: write three short reflections — a time you engaged with someone of a different view, a time you acted with courage, and a time you fell short.
For each, say what happened and what you learned in two or three sentences.
Q3: list eight true but unlikely facts about yourself, one line each.
Cut to the combined limits.
tips: The 'fell short' story should show real reflection, not a hidden boast.
avoid: Facts that are just achievements already on your résumé.
check: Q2 is 250 words or fewer combined; Q3 is 150 words or fewer.
steps.prompt: Reflect on three experiences (a different perspective, acting courageously, falling short), then give eight improbable facts about yourself.
steps.limit: 250 words combined (Q2); 150 words combined (Q3) — check the current application

steps.title: Write the 'connect the dots' essay
steps.why: The main essay shows who you are. KHS wants an essay so personal no one else could have written it.
do: List the people, places and events that shaped you.
Pick three or four that connect to each other and to who you are now.
Write a first draft without counting words.
Find the thread that links them and make it explicit.
Cut to 550 words and read aloud.
tips: Show, don't tell — scenes and details from your life beat summaries.
Your Nigerian or African context can be a strength when it is specific.
avoid: Turning it into a second résumé.
Using AI to write it — check the KHS policy on AI use.
check: It is 550 words or fewer and could only be about me.
steps.prompt: Connect the dots. How have the influences in your life shaped you?

steps.title: Choose and brief two recommenders
steps.why: KHS needs two letters tailored to its criteria, separate from your programme's letters.
do: Choose two people from academic, community or professional life who know you well (not family).
Ask them six weeks before the deadline.
Send them your résumé, essay draft and a note on the three criteria with stories they witnessed.
Register them in the KHS portal so each receives a personal link.
Remind them two weeks and three days before the deadline.
tips: Recommenders rate you on qualities like curiosity, courage and trustworthiness — ask for specific anecdotes.
avoid: Re-using your Stanford programme letter unchanged.
check: Both recommenders are registered and briefed.

steps.title: Complete and submit the KHS application
steps.why: The online form cannot be edited after submission, except a few items such as your résumé.
do: Fill every section of the KHS online application.
Upload résumé and transcripts; paste short answers and essay.
Proofread names, dates and programme choice.
Submit before 1:00pm Pacific Time on the deadline (that is 9:00pm in Nigeria) — there is no fee.
Save your confirmation.
tips: Submit even if letters are not all in yet — they can arrive by the deadline.
avoid: Missing the time zone — the deadline is US Pacific time.

steps.title: Submit your Stanford programme application
steps.why: You must be admitted to a Stanford programme. Its application is due by the programme deadline or 1 December, whichever is earlier.
do: Open your programme's application and complete it.
Upload its statement of purpose, letters, transcripts and test scores.
Pay the programme's fee (or check for a fee waiver).
Submit before the earlier of the programme deadline or 1 December.
tips: Tailor the statement of purpose to the programme; don't paste your KHS essay.
check: My Stanford programme application is submitted.

steps.title: Record the video statement if invited
steps.why: About 500 applicants are invited in January; videos are usually due 5–10 days after the invitation.
do: Watch your email throughout January.
The prompt: teach something to your cohort of fellow scholars, in two minutes or less.
Pick a topic you love — it need not be academic.
Practise, then record in the portal with your face visible.
tips: Production quality does not matter; clarity and personality do.
check: Video recorded within two minutes and submitted on time.

steps.title: Finalists: online interview and Immersion Weekend
steps.why: Up to about 180 finalists have a 25-minute Zoom interview in mid-February and attend Immersion Weekend at Stanford (5–6 March 2027), which includes a group interview.
do: Prepare behavioural stories for each of the three criteria.
Do two mock Zoom interviews.
Apply for your US visitor visa immediately — US visa waits in Nigeria can be long. KHS covers airfare, lodging and on-campus meals within university guidelines.
At Immersion Weekend, take part in both full days; listen and build on others' ideas in the group interview.
tips: Ask the KHS team straight away what visa support they can give finalists.

steps.title: Decision, Stanford offer and F-1 visa
steps.why: Scholars are notified on 16 March 2027. You also need your Stanford programme offer and an F-1 student visa.
do: Watch for the KHS decision and your programme decision (December–April).
Accept both offers by the dates given; KHS offers cannot be deferred.
Request your I-20 and book your F-1 visa interview early.
If not selected, reflect on which criterion was weakest and consider reapplying while still inside the degree-date window.
tips: Plan visa timing early — US visa interview waits can be long.
avoid: Assuming you can defer — you must reapply.

faq.q: Is there an application fee for KHS?
faq.a: No. Your Stanford programme usually charges its own fee.

faq.q: Does applying to KHS affect my Stanford admission?
faq.a: No. The two are evaluated separately, but you must be admitted to a programme to become a scholar.

faq.q: Is there a minimum GPA or test score?
faq.a: Not for KHS. You must meet your programme's requirements.

faq.q: Can I defer a KHS offer?
faq.a: No. If you cannot enrol that year you must reapply.

faq.q: Who pays for Immersion Weekend travel?
faq.a: KHS covers airfare, lodging and on-campus meals within university guidelines.

faq.q: I missed the October 2026 deadline. What now?
faq.a: The 2028-cohort application opens in summer 2027. Check the degree-date cutoff for that cohort.
